We are looking for a Power Electronics Engineer to take the lead on designing, modelling, prototyping and experimentally validating Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) converters and other multilevel power converter systems. The engineer will be responsible for the entire development process, including simulation, hardware realisation, testing and technical documentation, while also contributing to scientific publications and the generation of intellectual property. This role is pivotal to our efforts in advancing our high-efficiency, high-reliability power conversion technologies for applications such as renewable energy, motor drives and grid-tied systems.
 Your Responsibilities
 Take ownership of converter designs from concept through to prototype and validation
 Evaluate trade-offs in topology selection, device choice (e.g. silicon, silicon carbide, gallium nitride) and control strategies
 Develop detailed electrical and thermal models of NPC converters using tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS or LTspice
 Perform system-level simulations to evaluate converter performance under various operating conditions
 Design and implement advanced modulation and control schemes in firmware or DSP/FPGA
 Conduct experimental measurements including voltage/current waveforms, switching behaviour, thermal performance and total harmonic distortion analysis
 Prepare detailed technical reports summarising simulation results and experimental findings
 Collaborate on research papers and white papers and contribute to patent applications
 Work closely with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and researchers
 Your Qualifications & Skills
 Degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
 Previous experience in power converter development
 Expertise in multilevel converter topologies (especially NPC), gate drive design and protection
 Hands-on experience with simulation tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, PSpice or equivalent
 Good knowledge of programming languages such as Python and C
 Basic proficiency in building and testing power electronics hardware
 Familiarity with microcontrollers, DSPs and/or FPGAs is advantageous
 Passion for research and innovation, and a willingness to learn and adapt quickly
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English
 OUR COMMITMENT
 Innovative work environment in a young, dynamic team
 High-tech projects in the future-proof sector of e-mobility
 Opportunities for advancement in a growing company
 A wide range of further training opportunities
 Attractive bonus system and performance-related pay
 Additional company benefits 
 WHY ALPITRONIC
 Together with our customers, we are driving the world towards sustainable mobility – with cutting-edge technology, we inspire with the most innovative and reliable solutions. With our roots in South Tyrol, we are market and innovation leaders and set the future charging infrastructure standards from our locations in Bolzano/Bozen, Bergamo, Bologna, Munich and Charlotte (USA). 
 WHAT MAKES WORKING FOR US SPECIAL
 We are excited to meet individuals who are enthusiastic about making things happen, take personal responsibility and appreciate seeing the direct results of their work in the final product. We are a fast-growing company and offer our top teams a diverse and challenging range of tasks in a respectful corporate culture. Your contributions matter, are appreciated and have a significant impact! Join us and be part of our team!

Mission Senior BMS Test Engineer (EIS) H/F 
 Type de contrat : Mission pour freelance / portage salarial ou CDI
 Localisation : Toulouse
 Durée : 6 mois renouvelable
 Ref : 2470
 Nous 
 Avel Technologies est une société française de conseil en ingénierie et technologies, spécialisée dans les systèmes embarqués et le développement logiciel.
 Notre client est un acteur international du secteur des semi-conducteurs développant des solutions avancées pour les systèmes de gestion de batteries (BMS).
 Le contexte de la mission : 
 Au sein d’une équipe R&D basée à Toulouse, vous intervenez sur la validation et la caractérisation de nouvelles solutions BMS destinées aux cellules, modules et packs de batteries haute tension.
 La mission porte notamment sur le développement de bancs de tests automatisés basés sur la spectroscopie d’impédance électrochimique (EIS), la validation de systèmes d’excitation en courant utilisant des convertisseurs DC/DC ainsi que l’évaluation d’algorithmes d’estimation de l’état des batteries.
 La mission : 
 Concevoir, développer et maintenir des bancs de tests automatisés pour la caractérisation EIS de cellules et modules de batteries,
 Valider des circuits BMS intégrant des fonctions EIS ainsi que les éléments d’électronique de puissance associés,
 Mettre en œuvre et analyser des systèmes d’excitation en courant basés sur des convertisseurs DC/DC,
 Développer, calibrer et valider des algorithmes d’estimation SoH, SoC, SoP et SoT,
 Exploiter des modèles électriques équivalents de batteries (ECM) et des données expérimentales,
 Développer des traitements du signal pour l’extraction d’impédance : DFT/FFT, synchronisation, filtrage et analyse fréquentielle,
 Automatiser les essais, l’acquisition et l’analyse des données,
 Analyser les résultats de tests et identifier les anomalies ou écarts de performance,
 Rédiger les plans de tests, rapports de qualification et documentation technique,
 Participer aux démonstrations client et aux différentes étapes d’industrialisation..
 Compétences nécessaires : 
 Minimum 5 ans d’expérience en test batteries, validation BMS ou instrumentation électronique de précision,
 Formation ingénieur ou équivalent en électronique, systèmes embarqués, électronique de puissance ou domaine similaire,
 Expérience pratique des BMS et des systèmes de batteries Li-ion,
 Bonne maîtrise de la spectroscopie d’impédance électrochimique (EIS) et des modèles électriques équivalents (ECM),
 Expérience du test de modules ou packs batteries haute tension et de convertisseurs DC/DC,
 Maîtrise de Python et MATLAB/Octave pour l’automatisation des tests, le pilotage d’instruments et l’analyse de données,
 Connaissances en C/C++ embarqué,
 Solides connaissances en traitement numérique du signal : DSP, DFT/FFT, analyse fréquentielle et identification de systèmes,
 Compétences en debug électronique analogique / mixed-signal et instrumentation de précision,
 Capacité à travailler de manière autonome dans un environnement R&D international,
 Anglais courant.
 Formation initiale : 
 BAC+5, Master ou École d’Ingénieur en électronique, systèmes embarqués, électronique de puissance ou domaine similaire
 Key words : BMS, Battery Management System, EIS, Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy, Battery Testing, Battery Validation, Li-ion, High Voltage Batteries, Battery Pack, Battery Module, ECM, Equivalent Circuit Model, SoC, SoH, SoP, SoT, Test Automation, Test Bench, Python, MATLAB, Octave, C, C++, HIL, DC/DC Converter, Power Electronics, DSP, FFT, DFT, Signal Processing, Analog Electronics, Mixed-Signal, Electronic Instrumentation, System Identification

At Nova Sky Stories , we empower artists and producers to bring awe and wonder to live audiences around the world. As the global leader in drone entertainment , we’ve been redefining live shows for over a decade—merging cutting-edge drone technology with imaginative artistry.
With a veteran team of engineers and creatives, we design and operate lightweight, small, precise, and safe drones that perform in the most demanding environments—urban centers, extreme temperatures, and high winds. The result? Sky Stories that inspire, captivate, and transform the sky into a canvas of imagination.
Headquartered in the U.S. with teams across Europe and the UAE, Nova Sky Stories works with the world’s leading brands, venues, and events.
📱 Follow us: @NovaSkyStories
 About This Role
 Join our energetic and highly effective team with a start-up spirit in Gilching (near Munich)! We are building cutting-edge technology at the intersection of technology, art, and creative experiences. If you love solving tough challenges , working hands-on , and pushing technology forward with passion and fun , this role is for you!
At Nova Sky Stories there’s no daily hierarchy looking over your shoulder — you’ll take real responsibility for your projects, work independently, and deliver reliably. We’re looking for people who are self-reliant, hands-on, and genuinely excited about what they do.
 As a Flight Control Engineer (m/f/d), you’ll be responsible for: 
 Design and improve flight control algorithms and architecture for drones in challenging environments: strong wind, downwash, dynamic trajectories, high accuracy requirements 
 Develop embedded C/C++ software for onboard flight controllers (STM32).
 Build and validate algorithms using simulation, SIL, and HIL environments.
 Test your work in real flight conditions on tens and later hundreds of drones.
 Analyze flight data, tune parameters, and continuously improve system behavior.
 Help shape the technology powering one of the world's largest autonomous drone fleets.
 You’ll Need To Have
 Studying or recently completed a degree in Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Control Systems, or a related field.
 Strong understanding of control theory and flight dynamics.
 Experience with PID and at least one advanced control method (INDI, MPC, LQR, adaptive or learning-based control).
 Experience with sensor fusion or Kalman filters.
 Embedded C/C++ experience (STM32 is a plus).
 Python, MATLAB, or similar tools for simulation and analysis.
 Curious, hands-on, and excited to solve difficult engineering problems.
 Why Nova?
 Your work flies in live productions around the world.
 Own meaningful technical challenges from day one.
 Small, highly technical team with real autonomy.
 Startup culture where your ideas matter.
 Technology, engineering, art, and live entertainment all in one place.
 Ready to Show Us What You've Built?
 Forget perfect resumes.
Send us one, two, or three projects you're proud of—professional, academic, or personal—and tell us why they're interesting.
 If you're ready to play a key role in supporting the operational backbone of a company redefining storytelling in the sky, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now to help keep Nova Sky Stories flying high.

About Us 
 Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.
 Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.
 Overview 
Harmattan AI is developing new hardware products within the Launcher module: field-deployable drone launchers designed to be deployed and operated autonomously in demanding field environments. These products require dedicated electronics design with complex architecture in a constrained environment – PCBs integrating power conversion, energy management, control and communication interfaces – optimised for cost at volume. The Launcher team is seeking a dedicated hardware engineer to own electronics design end-to-end and accelerate the path to production milestones.
 Ideal candidate 
A senior hardware engineer who has designed and shipped complex PCBs, ideally mixing digital and significant power (hundreds of watts), into production. They are rigorous on schematics, layout, and bring-up, and have a strong instinct for cost and manufacturability. They design with real-world operating conditions in mind - temperature, moisture, surges - and an interest in battery thermal management; direct experience of outdoor-deployed equipment is a plus rather than a prerequisite. They are comfortable working autonomously in a small team and can bridge hardware and firmware.
 Skills required 
 PCB schematic and layout design (Altium Designer preferred)
 Power electronics design: ~300 W DC/DC conversion, protection, derating, efficiency and thermal budgets
 Thermal regulation: temperature sensing and control loops, battery storage temperature management, heatsinking
 Power over Ethernet (IEEE 802.3af/at/bt): combined power and data delivery, isolation, cable budgets
 Mixed-signal design: power management, MCU interfaces, communication buses (SPI, I2C, UART, USB, CAN, Ethernet)
 Hardware bring-up and debug: bench equipment proficiency
 DFM/DFA for PCB manufacturing and assembly
 Component selection and BOM management
 Experience in lightning and surge protection is a plus
 Responsibilities: 
 Schematic Design - Design complete schematics for mixed-signal and power boards, from power stages to digital and communication sections.
 PCB Layout & Routing - Perform or lead board placement and routing with attention to signal integrity, EMC, and power-path constraints.
 Power & Thermal Architecture - Define and validate the power architecture of the product and the thermal strategy, including battery temperature management.
 Environmental Robustness - Ensure the electronics withstand outdoor deployment conditions and define the associated qualification plan.
 Component Selection & BOM Optimization - Select components with cost, availability, and reliability in mind; drive BOM cost reduction for mass production volumes.
 Hardware Bring-up & Debug - Lead board bring-up, debug issues with oscilloscopes, power bench equipment, and other bench equipment; write bring-up scripts when needed.
 EMC & Safety Compliance - Address EMC challenges; ensure signal integrity across the board and electrical safety of the power and battery sections.
 Collaboration with Embedded SW - Work closely with the embedded software engineer to define hardware/software interfaces; support firmware bring-up.
 Collaboration with Mechanical - Ensure seamless PCB integration into mechanical enclosures (connectors, mounting, thermal, sealing, shielding).
 Supplier & Manufacturing Ramp-up - Qualify PCB manufacturers and assembly houses; support DFM/DFA review for production; manage NPI transitions.
 Documentation - Maintain schematics, layout files, test procedures, and hardware specifications.
 We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

About CynLr 
 Just like a baby’s brain, CynLr Visual Intelligence stack makes Robots to instinctively see & pick any object under any ambience, without any training. (a demo video link).
 Today, a robot that can fit a screw into a nut without slipping a thread, doesn’t exist. Imagine what it would take for a robot to assemble a Smartphone or a car by putting together 1000s of parts with varied shapes and weights, all in random orientations. Thus, factories become complex, needing heavy customization of their environment.
 CynLr-enabled visual robots intuitively learn to handle even unknown objects, on-the-fly, eliminating the need for rigid fixtures, pre-training, or environment customization. This enables an universal alternative to custom automation thus simplifying factory lines into modular LEGO-like micro-factories that can be rapidly reconfigured as products change.
 At the core of CynLr lies a fundamentally new approach to machine vision. Unlike conventional vision systems that rely on image recognition and heuristics, CynLr’ s Vision and ML stacks are deeply inspired by neuroscience, modelling how biological vision understands shape, geometry, and interaction rather than appearance alone. To support this, CynLr builds its hardware, sensors, compute pipelines, and learning stacks from scratch, tightly coupling perception, decision-making, and action.
 This integration allows CynLr to operate in conditions that defeat traditional automation: variable lighting, cluttered environments, unknown objects, and high precision manipulation, unlocking automation use cases that have remained unsolved for decades. By rethinking vision as an intelligent, adaptive sense rather than a static tool, CynLr is redefining how robots perceive, reason, and interact with the physical world.
 About The Role 
 A robot that works in the lab is a prototype. A robot that can be sold, shipped and trusted around people is a certified product. The gap between the two is made of standards, test evidence and engineering discipline.
 CynLr’s hardware spans an unusually wide range: the CLX dynamic stereo vision system with 400+ parts, the multi-arm CyRo robot, in-house robotic arms, high-power battery packs, and upcoming mobility platforms such as quadrupeds and AMRs. Each brings its own safety, EMC, battery and environmental requirements across India, EU/Switzerland and US markets.
 Certification cannot be an afterthought added at the end of design. It must shape architecture, component choices and test strategy from the first design review, so that every product reaches the market without costly redesigns.
 This role spans two broad scopes that work hand in hand. The first is Test Design : building the tests, rigs and evidence that prove our products work and are safe. The second is the Test & Certification Ecosystem : building the roadmaps, standards knowledge, and lab and regulator relationships that turn that evidence into certificates. Depending on your strengths, you may lead in one scope while contributing to the other. The Product Design, Battery & Power, and Mobility teams will be your internal customers.
 What You Will Do 
 Position 1 – Test Designer 
 Designing DVT, PVT and end-of-line test plans derived from product requirements and standards
 Designing and building test fixtures, automated test rigs and DAQ setups
 Running pre-compliance tests for EMC, electrical safety and environmental stress (thermal, vibration, shock, IP)
 Reliability testing (HALT/HASS, MTBF) and root-cause analysis of failures
 Test rigs for battery packs and for mobile-robot safety (stability, stairs, slopes, collisions)
 Position 2 – Test & Certification Ecosystem: 
 Building certification roadmaps for each product and target market
 Functional safety: risk assessments, safety requirement specifications, PL/SIL calculations, FMEA/FMEDA
 Building and managing relationships with external labs and notified bodies (TÜV, UL, Intertek, etc.)
 Tracking regulatory changes across India, EU/Switzerland and US
 Owning technical files, Declarations of Conformity and certification submissions
 Shared by both positions: 
 Embedding compliance and testability into design from day one
 Maintaining full traceability from requirement to test to certificate
 Acting as the test and compliance knowledge base for design engineers across the organization
 What Are We Looking For 
 Common to both positions 
 5–8 years in product test, certification or compliance for industrial automation, robotics, automotive, EV or similar electromechanical products.
 Clear technical writing for test reports, risk assessments and technical files.
 Working exposure to all of these standards areas:
 Robots and machinery: ISO 10218-1/-2, ISO/TS 15066, EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, IEC 60204-1, ANSI/A3 R15.06, UL 1740
 Functional safety: ISO 13849-1/-2, IEC 62061, IEC 61508
 Mobile robots: ISO 3691-4, ANSI/A3 R15.08, UL 3100
 EMC and radio: IEC 61000-6-2/-4, CISPR 11, EU RED, FCC Part 15, India WPC/TEC
 Batteries: IEC 62133-2, IEC 62619, UL 2271, UN 38.3, BIS IS 16046, EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542
 Environmental: IEC 60068, IEC 60529
 Position 1 – Test Designer: 
 Hands-on with oscilloscopes, power analysers, EMC pre-scan equipment and DAQ systems .
 Experience designing test fixtures and rigs , including basic mechanical and electrical design.
 Test automation in Python, LabVIEW or equivalent.
 Strong debugging and root-cause analysis skills.
 Position 2 – Test & Certification Ecosystem: 
 At least one product taken through CE, UL or equivalent certification end to end.
 Experience with functional safety analysis and documentation.
 Experience working with test labs, notified bodies and regulators , and managing certification timelines and costs.
 Good to Have: 
 TÜV Functional Safety Engineer certification or equivalent.
 Experience certifying battery packs or mobile robots.
 Exposure to vision or optical system testing.
 Team Structure & Growth 
 As mentioned earlier, this role spans two broad scopes that work hand in hand. The first is Test Design : building the tests, rigs and evidence that prove our products work and are safe. The second is the Test & Certification Ecosystem : building the roadmaps, standards knowledge, and lab and regulator relationships that turn that evidence into certificates. Depending on your strengths, you may lead in one scope while contributing to the other. The Product Design, Battery & Power, and Mobility teams will be your internal customers.
 Beyond specializing in the role of Test & Certification Engineers, this position offers growth into test, compliance and quality leadership roles as the organization scales. The Test Designer can grow into test architecture, test automation and reliability engineering; the Ecosystem engineer into functional safety, product compliance management and regulatory strategy.
 The role can also evolve into cross-functional and customer-facing opportunities such as supplier quality, customer audits, regulatory strategy for new markets and solution engineering, based on individual interests and business needs.

Who We Are
 Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards.
As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously.
We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications.
 The role
 Helsing delivers AI-powered capabilities that redefine machine perception and decision-making. Our technology powers a range of UAS platforms, accelerating critical mission functions.
You will work in a dedicated Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC) team and take full end-to-end responsibility for developing and validating state estimation, navigation and guidance algorithms. In close collaboration with field engineers, your goal is to elevate the performance of our UAS platforms to unprecedented levels and impact the future of defense technology.
The day-to-day
 Own the development of bespoke controllers for UAS end to end; through conception, design, simulation, physical integration and feature iteration.
 Design, test and implement state estimator algorithms that work robustly in contested environments
 Simulate the performance of navigation and guidance algorithms to inform the definition of sensor stacks, which could include IMUs, GPS/GNSS, barometers, magnetometers and advanced image-based positioning systems
 Analyse real sensor and test data to calibrate sensors and validate performance, closing the simulation-to-real gap
 Support the specification and execution of tests for navigation and guidance algorithm evaluation
 Collaborate with interfacing disciplines such as Flight Mechanics, Aerodynamics, Embedded Hard- and Software, and Testing
 Contribute to, follow and analyse flight tests
 You should apply if you
 Hold a M.Sc. or PhD in Aeronautical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics or an equivalent degree
 Have at least 5 years of professional experience in navigation, guidance or state estimation development
 Have very good skills in Matlab/Simulink
 Have a solid background in state estimation theory, aerodynamics, stability and control, and systems modelling
 Have excellent communication skills and the ability to report and present findings clearly and efficiently both internally and externally
 Possess solid software engineering skills, writing clean and well-structured code in Matlab and/or languages like Python, Rust, Java, or modern C++
 Are passionate about keeping up to date with current research and enjoy reimplementing / extending papers on state of the art navigation and guidance algorithms
 Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.
 Nice to Have
 Hands-on experience with fixed-wing aircraft / drones
 Have worked with or even contributed to open-source autopilots like Ardupilot or PX4
 Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields 
 Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns 
 The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world 
 Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation, be it reinforcement learning, distributed systems, generative AI, or deployment infrastructure. The defence industry is entering the most exciting phase of the technological development curve. Advances in our field of world are not incremental: Helsing is part of, and often leading, historic leaps forward 
 In our domain, success is a matter of order-of-magnitude improvements and novel capabilities. This means we take bets, aim high, and focus on big opportunities. Despite being a relatively young company, Helsing has already been selected for multiple significant government contracts 
 We actively encourage healthy, proactive, and diverse debate internally about what we do and how we choose to do it. At Helsing you will have a say in how we (and you!) work, the opportunity to engage on what does and doesn’t work, and to take ownership of aspects of our culture that you care deeply about

Our Mission 
Human time and effort is the rarest thing in the universe. The fact that so many people hate what they do for work is a disaster on so many levels. How many people live quiet lives of misery? How many generational talents do we miss due to circumstance?
 Dex’s mission is to close the gap between Talent & Opportunity, we believe that work, and being productive, is part of the human condition, that regardless of AI, human passion, ingenuity and a desire to do things means that work will always exist.
 We are building Dex to create a future where technology helps every individual to understand their strengths, interests and unique abilities, and to connect with opportunities where they can thrive, because more people doing things they love leads to a better, happier and more productive world.
We are starting by connecting the world's most ambitious software engineers with the companies that deserve them.
 The Role 
 This is a Staff-level full-stack product role with a backend-heavy centre of gravity. You'll own complete product slices end-to-end — things like a candidate database with rich search and filtering, a dashboard that surfaces call transcripts and match history for our Talent Operations team, and the workflows that let them stack-rank candidates against a new role in minutes rather than hours. You ship these without needing to be guided step by step.
 You're not a specialist who hands off at the API boundary. You think in user outcomes and delivery units, and you're reliable: your code handles edge cases, your APIs have clean contracts, and the work you ship stays shipped.
   What You'll Do 
 Own product delivery — take features from spec to production, backend-first but covering frontend and integration where needed
 Build and maintain backend systems — product APIs, data pipelines, and core infrastructure on our Python/FastAPI/Postgres stack
 Build with LLMs and agents — ship product features with significant LLM integration; contribute to the voice agent backend and information extraction systems
 Work across the stack — ship workable React/TypeScript frontend for product features; not a frontend specialist, but comfortable and pragmatic
 Collaborate with product and design — translate ambiguous requirements into concrete shipped work; be the engineer who unblocks, not the one who waits
 Maintain quality at speed — handle data integrity, error paths, API evolution, and operational concerns as a default, not an afterthought
   What We're Looking For 
 Leading teams or entire product lines - You can take responsibility for driving delivery across a team or across an entire product line
 Seeing good at scale, and early stage - you've moved fast in scrappy, early-stage environments, and seen what good looks like at scale
 Independent delivery - You can own and ship end-to-end product slices with minimal supervision; your track record shows features that shipped, stuck, and scaled
 Product trade-off judgment - you balance speed, quality, and user impact under ambiguity; you push back when something is underspecified and make pragmatic calls when it needs to ship
 Reliability and API discipline - you handle data integrity, error paths, idempotence, and API versioning as standard practice; production reliability is your default, not a later concern
 Cross-functional pragmatism - you work effectively with product and design, can unblock yourself across the stack, and ship workable frontend when that's what's needed
   Strong technical depth in: 
 Python backend (FastAPI or equivalent, async patterns, Postgres, Redis)
 LLM integration — building products where AI is in the critical path, not bolted on
 API design and data modelling
 JavaScript/TypeScript — comfortable enough to ship frontend features and review frontend PRs
   Nice to Have 
 Experience with voice agents or real-time audio pipelines
 Familiarity with evals, guardrails, or agent observability
 Familiarity with GCP / cloud infrastructure
 Experience in recruiting tech, marketplaces, or matching systems
   The Stack 
 A modern Python stack: FastAPI, Postgres, Redis, Docker, Pydantic AI , running on GCP. Frontend in React/TypeScript. We iterate fast and keep the codebase clean.
   What We Offer 
 Above market salary — we're building a world class team and believe pay should match that ambition
 Significant equity — we want this to be the last job you 'have' to take
 Full private healthcare & dental — because life happens and we want to support you
 Fertility benefits & enhanced parental support
 Gym membership & wellness benefits
 Claude tokens — lots and lots of Claude tokens
 Regular socials, offsites and an annual trip
 MacBook Pro + team kit
 "Whatever you need" approach to tools and support
 Interview process 
 We move quickly and with conviction. Broadly you can expect:
 We love it when candidates have experimented with our agent, Dex. Even if you aren't an Engineer, you can get a sense of what we're building, and we love to hear your feedback. 
 A 30m video call with our Internal Talent Lead; we'll share more about the team, role and business before asking questions about your experience and fit.
 Hiring Manager call: we'll share more specific context on short and medium-term objectives and ask deeper questions relative to the role requirements.
 Most roles involve a practical task to better understand how you work. Usually completed offline and reviewed by the team.
 Onsite interview loop where you'll visit the office, meet a cohort of the team, one interview centred on the task you produced, another on Dex culture and values, with a final interview with our Founder, Paddy.

PRIME FUNCTION
To ensure product and process quality in line with automotive industry standards by implementing robust quality systems, driving continuous improvement, managing customer requirements, and ensuring compliance with regulatory and organizational quality benchmarks.
 Job Description / Responsibilities
 Develop, implement, and maintain Quality Management Systems (QMS) in line with IATF 16949 / ISO standards
 Lead quality planning activities including APQP, PPAP, FMEA, Control Plans, and MSA
 Monitor manufacturing processes to ensure adherence to quality standards and specifications
 Handle customer complaints, conduct root cause analysis (RCA), and implement corrective & preventive actions (CAPA)
 Drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen methodologies
 Conduct internal audits, process audits, and supplier audits
 Ensure supplier quality through evaluation, development, and performance monitoring
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Production, Design, Supply Chain) for quality improvements
 Maintain documentation and records related to quality processes and compliance
 Train and mentor junior engineers and shop-floor personnel on quality standards and practices
 Ensure compliance with safety, environmental, and statutory requirements
 AUTHORITY
 Authority to stop production in case of major quality deviations
 Approve/reject incoming materials, in-process products, and finished goods based on quality standards
 Recommend process changes for quality improvement
 Initiate corrective and preventive actions across departments
 Interface with customers and suppliers on quality-related matters
 JOB SPECIFICATION / COMPETENCY
 Education:
 Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical / Automobile / Production Engineering
 Master’s degree or certification in Quality Management is an added advantage
 Experience:
 1-3 years of experience in quality roles within the automotive manufacturing industry
 Technical Skills:
 Strong knowledge of IATF 16949, ISO 9001 standards
 Hands-on experience with APQP, PPAP, FMEA, SPC, MSA
 Familiarity with core quality tools (8D, Fishbone, 5 Why, Pareto Analysis)
 Knowledge of GD&T and engineering drawings
 Experience with quality inspection tools and measurement systems
 Behavioral Competencies:
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
 Effective communication and stakeholder management
 Leadership and team collaboration
 Attention to detail and process orientation
 PERFORMANCE MEASURES
 Reduction in customer complaints and warranty claims
 First Pass Yield (FPY) / Right First Time (RFT) metrics
 Internal and external audit scores
 Supplier quality performance (PPM, rejection rates)
 Closure rate of CAPA within defined timelines
 Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) reduction
 Process capability indices (Cp, Cpk) improvement
 On-time completion of quality deliverables (PPAP, audits, etc.)
 Skills
 Competencies

Attentive Listening
Communicating Effectively
Customer Centricity

WHO WE ARE 
 Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.
 Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.
 Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.
 BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO 
 Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.
 Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.
 Design real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.
 YOUR IMPACT 
 As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you will significantly contribute to the design, analysis, validation and realisation of Proxima’s Alpha stellarator fusion machine. Your innovative and detailed engineering work will deliver robust mechanical, structural, and thermal performance of critical systems, tooling and manufacturing processes. You will also work with external collaborators and suppliers to develop the designs, equipment, systems and materials that will enable Proxima’s mission to deliver clean, sustainable fusion energy.
 WHAT YOU WILL DO 
 Develop innovative solutions and detailed mechanical designs for significant systems within the Alpha stellarator, ensuring integration with the broader physics, mechanical and structural systems.
 Carry out thermal and structural analysis and assessment of mechanical designs, providing design input and implementing recommended design improvements.
 Conduct technology trade-offs, materials selections and feasibility studies to facilitate the successful identification of the Alpha net energy stellarator.
 Design, deliver, and support the prototyping and verification of the components, materials, assemblies and manufacturing processes selected for Alpha.
 Work with external suppliers and collaborators to assist and guide the development and manufacture of the components and systems that will come together to demonstrate the net energy Alpha stellarator.
 WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR 
 High performers with excellent communication and problem-solving skills who love challenges and are not afraid to experiment, take risks, and learn from mistakes.

 Wir, der Battery Damage Service, sind ein führendes Unternehmen im Afterservice für industrielle Lithium-Ionen-Batterien. Unsere Dienstleistungen umfassen die Wartung und Instandhaltung, Logistik, Bergung sowie das Recycling dieser Batterien. Seit unserer Gründung im Jahr 2021 haben wir unser Serviceangebot kontinuierlich ausgebaut und optimiert. Als nachhaltig agierendes Unternehmen ermöglichen wir den sicheren und effizienten Einsatz von Batterien und tragen so zu einer umweltfreundlichen Zukunft bei. 
 Aufgaben 
 Du bereitest kontrollierte Entladevorgänge an industriellen Lithium-Ionen-Batterien vor und führst sie nach festgelegten Arbeits- und Sicherheitsanweisungen durch.
 Du überwachst die Entladeprozesse und prüfst sowie dokumentierst relevante Betriebs- und Messwerte.
 Du schließt die für die Entladung eingesetzten Prüf- und Entladeeinrichtungen an, bedienst und überwachst sie im Rahmen deiner Qualifikation und betrieblichen Freigaben.
 Vor, während und nach der Entladung führst du Spannungs- und Zustandskontrollen durch.
 Du erkennst Auffälligkeiten, Beschädigungen oder sicherheitsrelevante Abweichungen, bewertest sie und meldest sie unverzüglich.
 Du sicherst, kennzeichnest und dokumentierst entladene Batterien, Module und elektrische Komponenten.
 Du unterstützt bei der technischen Vorbereitung von Batterien für Wartung, Demontage, Weitertransport oder Recycling.
 Im Rahmen deiner Qualifikation führst du einfache elektrotechnische Prüf- und Dokumentationsaufgaben durch.
 Du arbeitest mit Demontage, Logistik, Disposition und weiteren operativen Bereichen zusammen.
 Bei der Weiterentwicklung von Entlade-, Prüf- und Sicherheitsprozessen wirkst du mit.
 Profil
 Eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung im Bereich Elektronik/Mechatronik oder eine vergleichbare fachliche Qualifikation wäre von Vorteil für dich.
 Du bringst Erfahrung im Umgang mit Mess- und Prüfmitteln (z.B. Multimeter) mit und verfügst über ein gutes technisches Verständnis.
 Deine Arbeitsweise ist sorgfältig, strukturiert und eigenständig.
 Du besitzt ein hohes Sicherheitsbewusstsein beim Arbeiten an elektrischen und energiereichen Systemen.
 Es fällt dir leicht, Arbeits-, Prüf- und Sicherheitsanweisungen konsequent einzuhalten.
 Du bist fähig, Messwerte und Prozessabweichungen aufmerksam zu beobachten und nachvollziehbar zu dokumentieren.
 Teamfähigkeit und klare Kommunikation im Arbeitsalltag zeichnen dich aus.
 Gute Deutschkenntnisse sind bei dir vorhanden für das sichere Verständnis von Arbeits-, Prüf- und Sicherheitsanweisungen.
 Optional sind Vorkenntnisse in den o.g. Aufgabenbereichen 
 Wir bieten
 Die Position bietet die Gelegenheit, verantwortungsvolle Aufgaben am Standort in Langelsheim zu übernehmen.
 Das Arbeitsumfeld ist von vielseitigen Tätigkeiten geprägt, die Batterietechnik, Instandhaltung, Demontage und Recycling umfassen.
 Eine strukturierte Einarbeitung in die technischen Abläufe und Sicherheitsstandards des Unternehmens gewährleistet einen fundierten Einstieg.
 Es besteht die Möglichkeit, technische Prozesse aktiv mitzugestalten und weiterzuentwickeln, wodurch Kreativität und Innovationsgeist gefördert werden.
 Die Arbeit findet in einer nachhaltigen und zukunftsorientierten Branche statt, die langfristige Perspektiven bietet.

 Please be advised that a valid work permit for Germany is required for non-EU citizens. Unfortunately, applications without a valid work permit and sufficient German language skills may not be considered.

About us 
 We see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. We invite you to join us in driving change with our fundamentally human-centered approach, uniting bright minds around a shared vision. The vision is: Prove to everybody that you can make a fundamental change. Prove with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects
 About our technology 
 The semiconductor industry’s growing demand for more powerful chips with higher bandwidth and lower power finds its solution in our technology. We connect chips to high-throughput, low-delay computing networks. The key lies in harnessing the physical properties of graphene to combine electronic computing with photonic communication, allowing countless chips to interact almost as if they were one. Our graphene photonic innovation increases computing power and efficiency to a new order of magnitude
 In short, we connect chips to create powerful and energy-efficient networks, overcoming connectivity limitations in the semiconductor industry. We deliver the graphene solution
   The Role 
 We are looking for a Layout Engineer to join our design team and support the development of layouts for photonic integrated circuits. You will maintain our layout infrastructure, help translate new designs into fabrication-ready layouts, and contribute to the implementation of new design rules and verification flows.
 To join our team, you should be excited to: 
 Maintain and further develop our layout libraries and workflows in Synopsys 
 Support designers in generating layouts for new photonic devices and circuits
 Run design rule checks (DRC) and layout-versus-schematic checks (LVS)
 Investigate and resolve DRC violations, off-grid errors, and other layout issues
 Implement new design rules 
 Assemble layouts 
 Support the mask flow from device layout through to mask data preparation
 Your Qualifications 
 Degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Photonics, or a related technical field
 Strong Python programming skills
 Understanding of integrated-circuit design; knowledge of photonic integrated circuits is preferred
 Experience with photonic layout software, ideally Synopsys OptoCompiler
 Experience with physical verification tools, ideally Synopsys IC Validator or a comparable platform
 Experience using KLayout
 Familiarity with DRC, LVS and mask-data preparation
 Our work culture 
 People Over Processes. At Black Semiconductor, flexibility is key—we ensure work adapts to life, not the other way around. We champion work-life harmony, where careers are meaningful and enriching. Our processes are human-centric, allowing you to focus on what matters
 Let’s grow together. Your potential is our priority. We provide the autonomy to make a lasting impact and nurture your growth through a culture of continuous learning. We invest in your journey for professional and personal development
 Your Health and Future Matter. Your well-being is paramount. We offer a comprehensive benefits package with outstanding insurance, pension and virtual stock options for your mental, physical, and financial health. Your peace of mind is our priority - in the present and future
 We Live Openness. Collaboration and inclusivity are the cornerstones of our culture. We practice openness, fostering trust and respect. Individuality is our collective strength, fueling innovation and driving us forward
 We connect chips – and people. We encourage qualified individuals from any background to apply. We foster an inclusive and supportive work environment that values collaboration, innovation, and growth. Join our team and be part of an organization dedicated to making a difference in the industry

Structural Engineer - Solar Arrays 
 Location: Germering, on-site
 About the hiring company: 
 Dcubed is a fast-growing space engineering company with the mission to make space engineering and exploration easy and accessible. What makes Dcubed special is that each of us is a space explorer at heart.
 At Dcubed, we enable the future of space missions with high-performance, flight-proven release mechanisms and deployable structures. From cutting-edge Release Actuators to scalable Deployable Solar Arrays and innovative Deployable Antennas, our technologies are designed for user friendliness, availability, and reliability — whether for smallsats in LEO or large missions to Moon, Mars and beyond.
 About the role 
 Space hardware must survive launch before it can perform its mission. Your analyses and tests will prove that it can.
 As Structural Engineer - Solar Arrays (f/m/d) , you will verify the structures and mechanisms that enable Dcubed's solar arrays to survive launch and deploy successfully in orbit. Through a combination of advanced simulation, first-principles engineering, and hands-on testing, you will turn ambitious designs into flight-ready hardware.
 If you enjoy understanding the physics behind complex systems, challenging assumptions, and validating your work through testing, this role is for you.
 Responsibilities 
 Perform structural analyses of solar arrays, deployable structures, mechanisms, and hold-down and release systems.
 Develop and validate FEM models for static, dynamic, thermoelastic, buckling, and non-linear analyses.
 Size composite and metallic structures, bonded joints, bolted interfaces, and inserts, and calculate structural margins of safety.
 Use analytical calculations and engineering judgement to cross-check simulation results and verify model assumptions.
 Support the design of lightweight structures and mechanisms capable of surviving launch loads and deploying successfully in orbit.
 Define and lead structural test campaigns, including vibration, static load, deployment, and thermal testing.
 Define loads, instrumentation, notching approaches, test predictions, and pass/fail criteria.
 Participate in test execution, investigate anomalies, correlate models, and support verification closure.
 Build and test coupons, prototypes, and representative hardware to generate material data and validate analytical models.
 Prepare structural analyses, test reports, and verification documentation, and support internal and customer reviews.
 Candidate Requirements 
 Experience & Qualifications 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related discipline.
 3+ years of experience in structural analysis and testing of aerospace, space, or other high-performance structures.
 Experience taking hardware from analysis through testing and verification.
 Experience with composite structures, deployable systems, mechanisms, or spacecraft hardware is highly desirable.
 Technical Skills 
 Strong understanding of structural mechanics, dynamics, vibration, and load-path analysis.
 Advanced FEM knowledge and strong experience with FEMAP and Nastran NX.
 Experience with Ansys and LS-Dyna is considered an advantage.
 Experience performing static, modal, random vibration, transient, buckling, thermoelastic, and non-linear analyses.
 Experience sizing composite and metallic structures, bolted joints, inserts, and bonded interfaces.
 Ability to assess structural margins and independently verify simulation results using first-principles calculations.
 Experience defining and executing structural test campaigns, including instrumentation, notching, and model correlation.
 Python, MATLAB, or similar tools for engineering calculations and data analysis.
 Familiarity with ECSS, NASA, or equivalent aerospace structural standards.
 Personal Attributes 
 Analytical, rigorous, and driven to understand the physics behind the results.
 Strong sense of ownership from analysis through successful test execution.
 Hands-on mindset with a willingness to prototype, instrument, and test hardware.
 Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
 Effective communicator and team player in a multidisciplinary environment.
 Comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment.
 Excellent English language skills.
 Eligibility to work in Germany
 What we offer 
 We want you to feel welcome and have the best possible tools for your work here at Dcubed. Therefore, we have selected a set of benefits to support your work days and everyday life, today and longer term.
 Commute: Deutschlandticket
 Wellbeing: EGYM Wellpass, recovery toolkit
 ETF-based pension program offering 30-50% company contribution
 Modern work equipment, based on your role and needs: laptop, phone, headphones, electric desk, wide screens, state-of-the-art workshop equipment
 Office environment: kitchen and break areas; lunch offering, beverages & snacks at the office; small exercise area, Space Bar
 Work-life balance & activities: hybrid work arrangements (location and working hours), company events and trips, launch parties
 Professional development: 70-20-10 thinking, training budget, training library, regular performance reviews
 Company swag: hoodie, t-shirt, stickers, water bottle, notebook etc.
 Interested? Apply here: https://dcubed.teamtailor.com/jobs/8434380-structural-engineer-solar-arrays-f-m-d

Who We Are
 Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards.
As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously.
We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications.
 The role
 You will build the simulation environments that support mission analysis for large satellite constellations, across hardware-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop. These environments let us test constellation software and real hardware on the ground, at pace, before anything reaches orbit. Engineering and programme decisions rest on them, so they must run fast, state their limits honestly, and earn the trust of the people who depend on them.
You will also contribute to mission and system design, and work with partners and suppliers whose models, hardware, and interfaces sit inside the same simulation.
 The day-to-day
 Build and maintain the simulation environments behind large constellation mission analysis. 
 Build hardware-in-the-loop rigs with real hardware in the loop, for example a flight computer or payload controller, and software-in-the-loop environments wired into our automated test and release pipelines. 
 Model the relevant physics, for example orbital and attitude dynamics, sensors, actuators, thermal behaviour, and RF links, at the fidelity each question demands. Validate those models against test and flight data. 
 Turn simulation results into trade studies, requirements evidence, and design recommendations the programme can act on. 
 Work with partners and suppliers to integrate their models and hardware, agree the expected fidelity, and resolve the discrepancies that surface once everything runs together. 
 You should apply if you
 Proven delivery of both software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop systems, including real hardware wired into a simulator. 
 Strong physics and modelling judgement. You can defend a simplification and sense where a model stops being trustworthy. 
 Several years of production-grade software work in a large, shared codebase, with code review, continuous integration, testing, and documentation. Python, plus at least one of Rust or modern C++. 
 The ability to architect one environment that serves both fast batch runs and full-fidelity wall-clock validation, including the real-time and scheduling trade-offs involved. 
 Confidence working across organisational boundaries, holding technical discussions with partners and suppliers, and explaining results, and their limits, to non-specialists. 
 Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.
 Nice to Have
 Optimisation background: design-space exploration, Monte Carlo and sensitivity analysis, trajectory or scheduling optimisation, or surrogate models. 
 Space domain exposure: orbit propagation, six degrees of freedom attitude dynamics, closed-loop AOCS simulation, or ground station, inter-satellite link, and payload models. 
 Distributed simulation standards, for example HLA, DIS, or FMI, or GPU and high-performance simulation. 
 Adjacent dynamic, safety-relevant domains, for example automotive, robotics, or autonomous systems, or consortium programmes involving model exchange between suppliers. 
 Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields 
 Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns 
 The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world 
 Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation, be it reinforcement learning, distributed systems, generative AI, or deployment infrastructure. The defence industry is entering the most exciting phase of the technological development curve. Advances in our field of world are not incremental: Helsing is part of, and often leading, historic leaps forward 
 In our domain, success is a matter of order-of-magnitude improvements and novel capabilities. This means we take bets, aim high, and focus on big opportunities. Despite being a relatively young company, Helsing has already been selected for multiple significant government contracts 
 We actively encourage healthy, proactive, and diverse debate internally about what we do and how we choose to do it. Teams and individual engineers are trusted (and encouraged) to practise responsible autonomy and critical thinking, and to focus on outcomes, not conformity. At Helsing you will have a say in how we (and you!) work, the opportunity to engage on what does and doesn’t work, and to take ownership of aspects of our culture that you care deeply about 
 What We Offer
 Competitive salary and VSOP options 
 Relocation support: up to €2,500 and 4 weeks temporary accommodation 
 Learning: €500/£450 yearly allowance 
 Health & wellness: gym membership and mental health support (Nilo.health) 
 Social: regularly company events and monthly social allowances 
 Enhanced parental leave: 22 weeks fully paid for primary caregivers & 6 weeks for secondary caregivers. 
 Family support: 5 days of paid family emergency leave, 100% remote work option during pregnancy and phased return to work 
 These are the core benefits across all locations, there may be additional benefits in certain locations.
 Helsing is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability or gender identity. Please do not submit personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, data concerning your health, or data concerning your sexual orientation.

 Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag inkl. Urlaubs- und Weihnachtsgeld
 Tarifliche Entlohnung nach dem GVP-Tarifwerk sowie ggf. Branchenzuschläge
 Hochwertige Profi-Schutz- und -Arbeitskleidung sowie arbeitsmedizinische Vorsorge
 Arbeitsplatzbezogene Weiterbildungen
 Mitarbeiter-Prämien zu besonderen Anlässen
 Vielzahl an Shopping-Rabatten
 Spannende Projekte bei wertschätzenden Kunden
 LEBENSLAUF GENÜGT:
Die Online-Bewerbung bei expertum dauert nur wenige Minuten. Einfach Lebenslauf hochladen, übernommene Daten überprüfen oder ergänzen und Bewerbung abschicken. Alternativ ist auch eine Bewerbung per E-Mail jederzeit möglich.
Wir freuen uns!

Responsable technique au sein d’un projet de Simulateur pour Contrôle Turbine.
Pour bâtir notre avenir, la meilleure énergie, c’est la nôtre!
Arabelle Solutions, filiale du Groupe EDF, est un leader mondial des technologies d’îlots turbines nucléaires, fournissant des solutions innovantes de production d’électricité bas carbone, allant de la turbine à vapeur la plus puissante au monde aux conceptions modulaires optimisées pour les SMR, ainsi que des alternateurs, pompes, échangeurs de chaleur et systèmes de contrôle. Ses technologies sont utilisées dans un tiers des centrales nucléaires mondiales et s’appuient sur une équipe de 3 500 experts répartis dans 16 pays.
Les piliers de notre culture déterminent la manière dont nous travaillons ensemble : Équipe, Expertise, Engagement.
Nous collaborons pleinement et valorisons l’esprit d’équipe, où chaque compétence est reconnue pour créer des solutions innovantes et efficaces. Guidés par la sécurité et l’intégrité dans tout ce que nous faisons, nous sommes engagés dans nos actions et nos résultats.
 Votre Rôle Et Impact Dans L’équipe
 Définir la structure du simulateur (MILHIL ou SIL) en fonction des besoins du projet.
 Assurer les rencontres techniques avec les clients (conseils fonctionnels et techniques).
 Réaliser la conception du simulateur (HIL).
 Assurer la programmation du simulateur de contrôle de la machine (contrôle de la régulation, des
 protections et des auxiliaires).
 Assurer la configuration IHM du simulateur.
 Gérer les essais en usine du matériel de simulation (logiciel applicatif et matériel) avant la réception
 avec le client.
 Gérer la réalisation et l'intégralité de la documentation complète du simulateur.
 Validation du DOW avec les autres entités le cas échéant.
 Coordination technique avec les autres produits A&C livrés sur un même projet.
 Supporter et / ou assurer le test de réception en l'usine avec le client final.
 Assurer le soutien de l'équipe de mise en service (voyage d'affaires dans un pays étranger possible).
 Soutenir le responsable technique dans l'utilisation du simulateur dans le test de la plate-forme.
 Votre Profil
 Formation :
 Diplôme d'ingénieur ou technicien (BTS ou DUT) spécialisé en simulation.
 Expérience
 Expérience technique de minimum 2 ans dans les systèmes de contrôle.
 Expérience dans les outils de simulation (MATLAB-Simulink, LabVIEW, ...)
 Compétences Comportementales Et Techniques
 Anglais courant.
 Esprit d'équipe.
 Orientée vers le client.
 Compétences en communication.
 Connaissances en Bond Graph.
 Connaissances de TestInView et/ou de VeriStand
 Nos Avantages
 Ce que nous offrons:
 Un environnement international et dynamique, engagé pour un avenir durable
 Culture d’entreprise collaborative tournée vers l’expertise
 Des avantages attractifs:
 Rémunération fixe sur 13 mois, et variable
 Intéressement
 Transport public : Prise en charge à 100% par l'entreprise
 Plan épargne salariale
 Télétravail : accord de 2j ou 3j par semaine
 Mutuelle (prise en charge par l’entreprise à 65%)
 Rejoignez une équipe engagée pour faire la différence en fournissant des technologies de pointe au service d’une énergie nucléaire durable.
Join us and work with global teams to support global customers ! At Arabelle Solutions, we have team members of more than 49 nationalities spread across 16 countries.
At Arabelle Solutions, we know diversity makes teams and business stronger.

items.jobTitle: Ingenieur (all genders) Elektrotechnik – Schwerpunkt Steuerungs- und Automatisierungstechnik
items.jobDescription:
Voll/Teilzeit
 Als Ingenieur (all genders) für Steuerschränke übernehmen Sie eine zentrale Rolle bei der Modernisierung und Zukunftssicherung der technischen Infrastruktur der Stadtreinigung Hamburg. Sie begleiten die sukzessive Erneuerung von rund 80 Bestandssteuerschränken und sorgen dafür, dass technische Anlagen auch künftig sicher, zuverlässig und wirtschaftlich betrieben werden können. Bewerben Sie sich bei Hamburgs beliebtestem Unternehmen!*
 Ihre Aufgaben
 Planung, Steuerung und fachliche Begleitung von Projekten zur Erneuerung und Modernisierung von Steuerschränken
 Entwicklung und Weiterentwicklung technischer Standards für Steuerschränke und zugehörige Steuerungstechnik
 Koordination und Überwachung der Umsetzung von Maßnahmen hinsichtlich Qualität, Kosten und Terminen
 Abstimmung mit internen Fachbereichen, insbesondere der Anlagentechnik und weiteren technischen Gewerken
 Steuerung und fachliche Begleitung von externen Planungsbüros, Dienstleistern und ausführenden Unternehmen
 Erstellung und Prüfung technischer Unterlagen, Ausschreibungen und Dokumentationen
 Durchführung von Abnahmen sowie Sicherstellung der technischen und normativen Anforderungen
 Aufbau und Sicherung von technischem Know-how im Bereich Steuerungs- und Automatisierungstechnik
 Ihr Profil
 Abgeschlossenes Studium der Elektrotechnik, Automatisierungstechnik, Mechatronik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung
 Erfahrung in der Planung, Errichtung oder Modernisierung von Schalt- und Steuerschrankanlagen
 Kenntnisse im Bereich Gebäude-, Betriebs- oder Anlagentechnik sowie der dazugehörigen Steuerungs- und Regelungstechnik
 Erfahrung im Projektmanagement und in der Zusammenarbeit mit externen Planungs- und Ausführungsfirmen
 Sicherer Umgang mit technischen Regelwerken, Normen und Vorschriften
 Ausgeprägte Kommunikations- und Koordinationsfähigkeit sowie ein hohes Maß an Eigenverantwortung
 Analytisches Denkvermögen, Organisationsgeschick und eine strukturierte Arbeitsweise
 Sicherer Umgang mit den gängigen MS-Office-Anwendungen
 Unser Angebot

 Work-Life-Harmony: 30 Tage Jahresurlaub, Home-Office Möglichkeit, Gleitzeit 
 Gesundheit: Umfangreiches Angebot des betrieblichen Gesundheitsmanagements sowie vergünstigte Mitgliedschaft beim Urban Sports Club
 Familienfreundlichkeit: Hohe Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Privatleben
 Weiterentwicklung: Umfangreiche Trainings- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten 
 Verpflegung: Preiswertes und hochwertiges Essen in unseren Kantinen 
 Gemeinschaft: Gutes Betriebsklima und kollegiales Miteinander 
 Mobilität: Attraktives Fahrradleasing, Zuschuss zum Deutschland-Ticket

items.jobTitle: Systems Simulation & Performance Modelling - Member of Technical Staff
items.jobDescription:
About Us 
 We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.
 Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.
 The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.
 Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.
 Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.
 In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.
 We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.
 About the Role 
 Callosum believes that scaling heterogeneous AI infrastructure requires understanding how emerging hardware will behave as part of larger computational systems. Performance characteristics measured on individual accelerators rarely translate directly to distributed deployments, where networking, memory, and execution strategies introduce new constraints. We are developing simulation infrastructure that allows us to explore these interactions and evaluate future systems before they exist.
 This role advances the simulation and performance modelling tools that inform Callosum's hardware and infrastructure decisions. You will extend models that project device-level performance to rack-scale systems, explore alternative hardware configurations and execution strategies, and provide experimental environments for automated optimisation. The work also encompasses profiling, workload tracing, and performance instrumentation, connecting measurements from real systems to accurate and useful models of those we want to build.
 What You'll Build 
 Extend our simulators to predict heterogeneous compute performance from individual accelerators to multi-rack deployments.
 Model networking, memory, and execution behaviour to evaluate alternative system architectures and configurations.
 Develop profiling, tracing, and workload capture tools that inform and validate simulation models.
 Extend simulation environments for rapid experimentation and automated optimisation of systems and algorithms.
 Characterise emerging accelerator architectures and translate hardware measurements into predictive models of system-level performance.
 What Sets You Apart 
 Strong experience in systems simulation, performance modelling, or performance-critical systems software.
 Deep understanding of computer architecture, distributed systems, or high-performance computing.
 Familiarity with profiling, tracing, instrumentation, and methods for characterising computational workloads.
 Strong systems programming experience, ideally including C++ or Rust.
 Ability to reason about modelling accuracy, abstraction, and trade-offs between simulation fidelity and computational cost.
 What We Offer 
 Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience
 Equity & Ownership
 Private healthcare
 We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world
 We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us
 We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome, and believe in equal opportunities for all.

items.jobTitle: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
items.jobDescription:
The question 
 Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. 
 What you will do 
 The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 
 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 
 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 
 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 
 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements. 
 A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement.
 Who we are looking for Required 
 • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract. 
 • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models. 
 • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure. 
 • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI. 
 • Working English; French is not required. 
 Valued, not required 
 Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply.
 What matters most 
 We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator.
 What we offer 
 • A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot. 
 • A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design. 
 • Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI). 
 • Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers. 
 • Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling. 
 Conditions 
 Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment.
